newsitem.title: ITALY: At least five feared dead in Italy train accident.
newsitem.headline: At least five feared dead in Italy train accident.

text.p: At least five people were feared dead in northern Italy after an express train hurtled off the track on Sunday, police said.
Another 50 were injured when the Milan-Rome "Pendolino" (tilting train) derailed as it was approaching the station of Piacenza, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Milan.
"The train was going very fast and all of a sudden we found ourselves lying sideways -- it was terrible," a member of the crew told Italian radio.
The conductor, assistant conductor, and a number of other people were trapped in the wreckage.
A police official on the scene told Italian television five people were killed in the derailment and at least two others were feared dead.
The Pendolino is a highly popular fast train that makes the run between Italy's two most important cities in around four hours.
Former Italian president Francesco Cossiga was aboard the train but escaped unhurt. "I heard a big bang and all of a sudden I was on the floor," he told reporters.
The train had left Milan at 1230 GMT and was due to arrive in Rome at 1620 GMT.
The accident blocked rail traffic in both directions on the main north-south link.
